quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: If road conditions require longer stopping distance than normal, you should:

options.text: Decrease your usual following distance.
Increase your usual following distance.
Travel on the shoulder.
Ask someone else to operate your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your usual following distance.
questions.explanation: When your motorcycle needs more distance to stop, increase your following distance. Use a minimum three-second gap if the road is slippery, if you cannot see ahead clearly, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: Do not change gears on railroad tracks because:

options.text: Your motorcycle may stall.
You might go too fast.
Other drivers may not be expecting you to change gears.
The uneven surface may make it more difficult to switch gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may stall.
questions.explanation: Do not shift gears while crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle could stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: If the throttle is stuck, you should:

options.text: Jump off the motorcycle.
Apply the brakes.
Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If your throttle is stuck, twist it back and forth several times to free it. If this does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Use your high beam.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
Be visible.
Ride only in the left portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride only in the left portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: At night, use your high beam, use other vehicles' headlights to help you see, and wear reflective clothing. Move around your lane to see better, be seen better, and stay safe from other traffic.

questions.question: When stopping, it is best to:

options.text: Grab at the front brake lever.
Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
Apply increasing pressure to the rear brake.
Only use the front brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank and keep your eyes up.
questions.explanation: For a good straight-line stop, apply the brakes smoothly and firmly. As your weight moves forward, increase pressure on the front brake and decrease pressure on the rear brake. Keep your knees against the gas tank and look ahead to stay in a straight line.

questions.question: During acceleration, a sidecar attached to a motorcycle will:

options.text: Feel like it is lagging behind.
Feel like it is accelerating faster than the motorcycle.
Vibrate uncontrollably.
Make acceleration seem faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel like it is lagging behind.
questions.explanation: A sidecar is an unpowered weight attached to your motorcycle. When you accelerate, it feels like the sidecar is falling behind because of its weight and inertia.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Shift your weight quickly.
Turn the handlebars quickly.
Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
Press the handle grip in the direction opposite of where you plan to swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handle grip in the direction you plan to swerve.
questions.explanation: To swerve around a hazard, push gently on the handle grip in the direction you want to go. To swerve left, push the left grip, then push the right to straighten out. To swerve right, push the right grip, then the left.

questions.question: To best control a motorcycle, a rider should:

options.text: Sit with their arms fully extended.
Use their arms to hold their body up.
Keep their knees away from the gas tank.
Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep their feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle, not support your body. Keep your arms slightly bent. For better balance, keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: If you are riding when it starts to rain, it is a good idea to:

options.text: Ride down the center of the lane.
Increase your speed.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Pull onto the shoulder of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: The center of a lane has oil deposits that make it slippery when wet. When rain starts, ride in the tire tracks left by cars. Also, slow down on wet roads.

questions.question: When entering a highway or curve, motorcyclists riding in a group should:

options.text: Ride single-file.
Ride in a staggered formation.
Ride in pairs.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride single-file.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for group riding, but switch to single-file when turning, going through curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press the right handgrip.
Press the left handgrip.
Press both handgrips at the same time.
Not press either handgrip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the left handgrip.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. To lean in the direction you want to go, press the handgrip on that side.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, you may need to adjust all of the following, except:

options.text: Tire pressure.
Mirror positions.
Headlight position.
Brake light position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake light position.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle sits differently with a passenger because of the extra weight. You may need to adjust tire pressure, suspension, shocks, headlight, and mirrors. You do not need to adjust the brake light position.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, you should:

options.text: Speed up before impact.
Slow down before impact.
Lean the motorcycle.
Stay seated on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before impact.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an object, slow down as much as you can. Try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Keep the motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and ease off the throttle before impact.

questions.question: Which of the following is true?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal braking power.
The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
The rear brake provides more braking power than the front brake.
Only the front brake should be used when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and provides at least 70 percent of the stopping power. Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.question: As the motorcycle's weight moves forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can apply the front brake harder.
Should use less pressure on the front brake.
Can apply the rear brake harder.
Lose traction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: When you brake, your weight shifts forward. This gives the front wheel more grip. You can then press the front brake harder.

questions.question: Motorcycle riders:

options.text: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
Should only wear hearing protection on long rides.
Should not wear hearing protection because it will block important sounds like horns and sirens.
Do not need hearing protection if they wear a full-face helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should wear hearing protection at all times to prevent hearing damage.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can cause permanent hearing damage, even with a full-face helmet. Ear plugs and other hearing protection help prevent damage while still allowing you to hear horns and sirens.

questions.question: When going through a curve, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same portion of the lane.
Always stay in the left portion of the lane.
Always stay in the right portion of the lane.
Remember that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remember that the best path may not follow the curve of the road.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change. Be ready to change your lane position as needed. The best path through a curve may not follow the road's curve exactly.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be seen easily.
Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
Is recommended because a passenger may tell the driver you are there.
Is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane where the driver is most likely to see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: When looking through a turn to see where you are going, you should:

options.text: Turn just your head.
Turn your head and shoulders.
Turn just your shoulders.
Turn your entire body.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to see where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, you will want to adjust the:

options.text: Brakes.
Seat.
Suspension.
Brake light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Suspension.
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to the settings recommended for that weight.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: Traffic is light.
Traffic is heavy.
You can see the road through vehicles in front of you.
The weather is clear and pleasant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic is heavy.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when conditions make it harder to stop. This includes heavy traffic, wet roads, poor weather, and nighttime driving. Also increase it if you cannot see around the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular?

options.text: School crossing sign.
Railroad crossing sign.
Stop sign.
Speed limit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: How do you stop another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage drivers from trying to share it with you.

questions.question: How should you look through a turn while riding?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your arms straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look where you want to go through the turn. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: The center of the lane has an oily strip. What should you do?

options.text: Try to avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
Ride only on the oily strip for better grip.
Avoid the entire center portion of the lane.
Do not worry about oil or debris in a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Try to avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from vehicles collects in the center of lanes. On dry roads, this strip usually provides enough grip for motorcycles. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it while staying in the center portion of the lane. Avoid it when the road is wet.
